title: Polynomial base change and constant polynomial bases of a finite locally free algebra
statement:
Let $A,B$ be commutative rings, $\varphi:A\to B$ unital, and $p:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ finite locally free of degree $r\ge0$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-finite-locally-free]. Suppose $f_1,\ldots,f_m\in A$ generate $A$ as an ideal and $e_{i,1},\ldots,e_{i,r}$ are bases of $B_{f_i}$ over $A_{f_i}$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away, def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Write $C$ for inclusion as constant polynomials and $\varphi[T]:A[T]\to B[T]$ for the coefficientwise extension [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. The canonical ring isomorphism
$$B\otimes_A A[T]\xrightarrow{\sim}B[T],\qquad b\otimes\sum_j a_jT^j\longmapsto\sum_j b\varphi(a_j)T^j$$
[def-weil-module-base-change] identifies $\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi[T])$ with the base change $\operatorname{Spec}B\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}A[T]\to\operatorname{Spec}A[T]$ of $p$ along $\operatorname{Spec}A[T]\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. This morphism is finite locally free of degree $r$, and its structure-sheaf pushforward is quasi-coherent and locally free of rank $r$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. The elements $g_i=C(f_i)$ generate the unit ideal of $A[T]$. The coefficientwise localization maps give compatible isomorphisms
$$A[T]_{g_i}\cong A_{f_i}[T],\qquad B[T]_{g_i}\cong B_{f_i}[T],$$
under which $C(e_{i,1}),\ldots,C(e_{i,r})$ are bases over $A_{f_i}[T]$. The assertion includes zero rings, an empty cover of the zero ring, and $r=0$.

proof.text: Use polyEquivTensor_symm_apply_tmul for the explicit tensor formula [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension]. For the cartesian square, Polynomial.algebra and its Algebra.IsPushout instance identify B[T] as the pushout of B and A[T] over A. CommRingCat.isPushout_of_isPushout and isPullback_SpecMap_of_isPushout turn that ring pushout into the displayed affine pullback [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. Both algebra maps are definitionally the displayed C and coefficientwise polynomial map.

source.place: polyEquivTensor_symm_apply_tmul and polynomial Algebra.IsPushout instances; Tag 01I4

proof.text: Base change along the polynomial C map preserves finiteness, flatness, and local finite presentation [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence, lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Combine the three instances to obtain finite local freeness [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. The exact source-library formula Scheme.Hom.fiberDegree_of_isPullback gives the degree of the new fibre as the old fibre degree. This is the affine fibre-product description followed by invariance of vector-space dimension under residue-field extension [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra, lem-pc-finrank-field-base-change]. Apply the degree-r hypothesis.

The polynomial morphism is affine, so its structure-sheaf pushforward is quasi-coherent by Scheme.Modules.isQuasicoherent_pushforward_of_isAffineHom [lem-pc-affine-morphism-hi]. Its finite local freeness of rank r follows immediately from Scheme.Modules.isFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank_pushforward_unit [lem-pc-flf-properties] and the degree-r result of the preceding step. These existing proved source-library statements include the associated-sheaf and local-basis arguments; no new tilde/Gamma comparison is needed.

Apply Ideal.map C to the hypothesis Ideal.span (range f) = top. Ideal.map_span, Ideal.map_top, and range of a composite give exactly that the constant polynomials C(f_i) span the unit ideal [def-weil-polynomial-ring].

source.place: Tag 02DV(3), extension of the unit-ideal equation

proof.text: For R and a in R, the Mathlib theorem Polynomial.isLocalization identifies R_a[T] as the localization of R[T] at the image of the powers of a. Submonoid.map_powers identifies this submonoid with the powers of C(a). By uniqueness of localization [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-universal-property, def-weil-ring-localization-away], IsLocalization.algEquiv supplies the comparison from Localization.Away (C(a)), and its commutes equation gives the asserted formula on every numerator polynomial. Apply this once to (A,f_i), and once to (B,phi(f_i)); Polynomial.map_C identifies the second localization parameter. Compatibility follows by IsLocalization.ringHom_ext: after precomposing with the numerator map, the square is equality of coefficientwise maps, and their coefficient ring homomorphisms agree by IsLocalization.map_eq. This proof uses no nonzero-divisor hypothesis.

For any R-algebra S with basis b, use the polynomial pushout with the scalar factors interchanged. Its IsBaseChange datum and IsBaseChange.basis transport b to an R[T]-basis of S[T] [lem-weil-pbc-free-module-base-change-free, lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension]. IsBaseChange.basis_apply says that its vectors are exactly C(b_j). Apply this with the explicitly specified localized coefficient algebra structure and the given basis e_i. All constructions work for empty basis, zero localizations, and zero rings; no additional assumptions are introduced.
